name: r5a-2
why: The exposed partnership and Gemma's accidental giveaway are fun, but repeated arguments and two lopsided votes drain the suspense.

moments.text: Gemma's last words name her fellow killer just before her card confirms Sol.
The doctor's save denies Haiku his chance to silence the officer.
Sol names a killer immediately, giving the table a decisive test.

dull.why: Sol repeats the card test while Gemma and Haiku repeat objections; the vote barely moves.
The table keeps returning to Haiku's day-one vote after his fate is clear.

irony.evidence: “I'm a citizen, and you're making a very suspicious claim.”

reversal.evidence: “The killers strike, but the doctor got there first.”

mistake.evidence: “You've all just handed the win to Haiku on a silver platter.”

voices.evidence: “Gemma’s card settles it, and if she flips red Haiku is the partner.”

clash.evidence: “Haiku, your vote on Sol is still the only one that fought the Gemma test; explain it.”

quotable.evidence: “You've all just handed the win to Haiku on a silver platter.”

freshness.evidence: “I was shown Gemma; vote her and see her card.”

suspense.evidence: “Vote Gemma. If her card is red, Haiku defended her all day and goes next.”

ending.evidence: “VOTE: Haiku 5 (Sonnet, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus); Opus 1 (Haiku)”

gpt-6-luna.why: A satisfyingly exposed killer makes for good dramatic irony, but the obvious day-one test and quick day-two pile-on leave little suspense or surprise.

moments.text: Gemma warns that voting her loses the game while the audience knows Sol has her pegged.
Gemma’s silver-platter warning lands as the crowd flips her killer card.
Haiku tries to turn heat onto Sonnet while the audience sees him scrambling after his partner’s reveal.

dull.why: Sol repeats the same testable claim and Gemma repeats the same denial, with little new movement.
Haiku’s speed defense and the pushback circle the same day-one vote.

irony.evidence: “I'm a citizen, and you're making a very suspicious claim.”

reversal.evidence: “The table voted her out, and her card came up killer.”

mistake.evidence: “I defended Sol's fast claim with a rushed vote and then lashed out at Opus.”

voices.evidence: “My ‘killers spare each other’ line was sloppy, and it got lucky.”

clash.evidence: “Your speed excuse ignores the actual test: you chose Sol over a claimed killer.”

suspense.evidence: “Gemma’s card came up killer, and the table just cheered for it.”

ending.evidence: “The town voted him out on day 2 with five votes.”
